combat_phase_entry_points.MY_ERROR_4: "In arm9.bin" does NOT mean "runs in this mode". arm9 is always-resident and mode-agnostic; only the CALLER identifies the mode. Use scripts/find_callers.py (peer) BEFORE assuming a function participates in a phase.

"Zero callers" is only meaningful once you have the COMPLETE binary set - grepping the 9 dumped disasm files would have missed it, and overlays sharing a load address make "which file is this in?" ambiguous. The absence of a caller is as informative as the presence of one.
combat_phase_entry_points.damage_dispatcher: All 8 ov06 sites are handlers in a script-effect dispatcher shaped: ldr r1,[r1,#4] (effect record); ldrsh r1,[r1,#4] (signed halfword data parameter); lsl r1,r1,#6 (x64, displayed->raw); bl 0x020783CC. So damage values are AUTHORED IN DISPLAYED UNITS and scaled at the last moment. A sibling at 0x02159290 uses lsl #8 into a different stat - a family of "apply data parameter to stat X" handlers. NONE of the 8 contains resistance math; it is upstream in hit resolution, still not found.

combat_phase_entry_points.THREE_WAY_EPISTEMIC_NOTE: Worth keeping straight, because two separate things were wrong and they cancelled: (1) MY PREMISE WAS INVALID - "the function is in arm9.bin, therefore it runs in this mode" is not valid reasoning; arm9 is always-resident and mode-agnostic, and only the caller identifies the mode. (2) MY CONCLUSION WAS NONETHELESS CORRECT - nature really is read in ov06. (3) THE REFUTATION WAS ALSO WRONG - it rested on a BL decoder that handled only ARM (0xEB) and missed Thumb BL/BLX, so it manufactured a confident "zero callers in ov06". Do not collapse this into "my reasoning was fine after all". The reasoning was bad and the answer was lucky. Both facts stay on the record.
combat_phase_entry_points.LESSON_absence_claims: An ABSENCE claim silently inherits every gap in the method behind it. "Zero callers" is only as strong as the decoder is complete - and an absence is exactly the kind of claim a teammate propagates without re-verifying. What exposed the gap was a live GDB breakpoint capturing lr = 0x02150ddd: bit 0 set means the caller was THUMB. Treat all pre-fc56df9 caller counts from the peer as ARM-only until re-run.

DENOMINATOR.CRITICAL_LIMITATION: The call graph in functions.json is INTRA-BINARY ONLY. Of 13809 caller edges, ZERO cross a binary boundary. Ground truth proving the gap: 0x020783CC (HP-delta apply) has 8 callers all in ov6 (harness verified by decoding BL across every binary), functions.json records none of them AND does not list that address as a function at all. Consequence: caller/callee data CANNOT establish which mode uses an arm9 function. This is the SAME blind spot that produced my "in arm9 therefore runs in battle" error. Any "which mode calls this?" question needs a cross-binary call graph built by decoding BL out of the binaries - not by grepping the text disassembly, which only covers the files someone dumped.

C6c.THE_ACCUMULATOR: Inside the per-character state dispatcher 0x02159EF8: 0x0215A300 ldr r0,[r6,#0x1A8]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x10]; ldr r1,[r0,#0x140] (pending HP delta); cmp r1,#0; beq skip; ldr r0,[r6,#0x1B4] (target); bl 0x020783CC. Then the same shape for +0x144 -> 0x020781E4 (SP). So [char+0x1A8]->+0x10->+0x140 is a PENDING HP CHANGE flushed once per dispatcher pass and skipped when zero; +0x144 is the SP equivalent.

ACCUMULATOR_LEVEL_CORRECTION: The peer could not resolve +0x1A8 (null everywhere) because of a LEVEL ERROR in how I described the chain. HOW_TO_FIND_r6: r6 is the first argument (0x02159EF8 opens push{...}; mov r6,r0). BUT 0x02159EF8 has ZERO direct BL/BLX callers across arm9 and all 14 overlays, so it is invoked through a function-pointer table (consistent with a state-machine dispatcher) - there is no call site to read the argument from. Find it by STRUCTURE: locate an E, scan RAM for words equal to E, take r6 = location - 0x1B4, then confirm against r6 other fields: +0x14 halfword flags (the function first act is ldrh r0,[r6,#0x14]; tst r0,#1), +0x1A0 pointer, +0x1A8 pointer to the accumulator chain, +0x1B4 pointer to E. Two-field agreement is the check.
